title: Machine Learning & Deep Learning
subtitle: From linear models to Transformers, with the mathematics behind them
audience_line: Developers, analysts and engineers who want to build machine learning models
overview: This programme teaches participants to build, evaluate and explain machine learning models, and the mathematics that makes them work. They cover supervised learning, from linear and logistic regression to trees, ensembles and support vector machines, with sound evaluation, tuning, pipelines and experiment tracking; unsupervised learning; and deep learning, from a network built from scratch to PyTorch, CNNs, attention and the Transformer. A responsible AI phase covers explainability, fairness and governance, an optional reinforcement learning module adds 9 h, and the programme closes with an end-to-end machine learning project presented by each team.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Developers, analysts and engineers who want to build machine learning models

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Python, NumPy and pandas (course: Python for Data Science), or equivalent; secondary-school algebra. The mathematics needed is taught in the course

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 75 h: 66 h of chapters + 9 h buffer; optional reinforcement learning module: +9 h

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Lectures that derive each method, followed by labs in Jupyter; the mathematics is taught where it is used

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant (16 GB RAM, Python 3, JupyterLab, scikit-learn, PyTorch, MLflow); GPU notebooks on Google Colab or a GPU server provided by the organiser for deep learning; no paid cloud account

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can frame a machine learning problem, build and compare classical and deep learning models, evaluate them without leakage, explain their predictions and track the experiments

phases.name: Supervised Learning
phases.focus: Regression, classification, trees, ensembles, SVMs, evaluation, pipelines
phases.intro: Participants learn how a model generalises and how to measure it honestly, then build the main supervised methods from their mathematics: linear and logistic regression trained by gradient descent, decision trees and ensembles, and support vector machines. They finish with cross-validation, hyperparameter search, feature pipelines and experiment tracking with MLflow. Validated lab: a tuned scikit-learn pipeline compared with two baselines on a held-out test set, with every run tracked in MLflow.

chapters.title: Framing & Linear Regression
chapters.content: Regression vs classification, generalisation, data splits, data leakage; vectors, matrices, normal equation

chapters.title: Gradient Descent & Regularisation
chapters.content: Derivatives, chain rule, gradient descent, ridge and lasso

chapters.title: Logistic Regression & Metrics
chapters.content: Sigmoid, maximum likelihood, cross-entropy, precision, recall, ROC

chapters.title: Decision Trees
chapters.content: Entropy, information gain, Gini impurity, CART

chapters.title: Ensembles
chapters.content: Bagging, random forests, boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM)

chapters.title: Support Vector Machines
chapters.content: Margins, soft margin, kernels, SVR

chapters.title: Evaluation & Tuning
chapters.content: Cross-validation, learning curves, grid, random and Bayesian search

chapters.title: Feature Engineering & Pipelines
chapters.content: Encoding, scaling, scikit-learn pipelines, MLflow tracking

phases.math: Linear algebra (vectors, matrices, normal equation) · Calculus (derivatives, chain rule, gradient) · Statistics (maximum likelihood, cross-entropy, bias and variance) · Information theory (entropy, information gain) · Optimisation (convexity, gradient descent, L1 and L2 penalties, constrained optimisation for the SVM margin, kernels)

phases.name: Unsupervised Learning
phases.focus: Clustering, mixture models, PCA, manifold learning, anomalies, recommenders
phases.intro: Participants find structure in data without labels: hierarchical, density-based and centroid clustering, Gaussian mixtures trained with expectation-maximisation, dimensionality reduction with PCA, t-SNE and UMAP, anomaly detection, association rules and collaborative filtering. Validated lab: a customer segmentation with K-Means and a Gaussian mixture, visualised after PCA, with the choice of the number of clusters justified.

chapters.title: Unsupervised Framing
chapters.content: Clustering, density estimation, dimensionality reduction

chapters.title: Hierarchical Clustering & DBSCAN
chapters.content: Linkage criteria, density-based clustering

chapters.title: K-Means & Gaussian Mixtures
chapters.content: Objective function, Lloyd’s algorithm, expectation-maximisation

chapters.title: PCA
chapters.content: Covariance, eigendecomposition, explained variance

chapters.title: Manifolds & Anomalies
chapters.content: t-SNE, UMAP, isolation forest

chapters.title: Association Rules & Recommenders
chapters.content: Apriori, support, confidence and lift, collaborative filtering

phases.math: Probability (multivariate Gaussian, expectation-maximisation) · Linear algebra (covariance matrix, eigendecomposition) · Distances and similarity measures

phases.name: Deep Learning
phases.focus: Neural networks from scratch, backpropagation, PyTorch, CNNs, attention and Transformers
phases.intro: Participants build a neural network in NumPy to see every step, derive backpropagation, then train models with PyTorch: convolutional networks and transfer learning for images, recurrent networks for sequences, attention and the Transformer architecture. Validated lab: an image classifier fine-tuned from a pretrained CNN in PyTorch, with its training curves and checkpoints.

chapters.title: Perceptron & MLP from Scratch
chapters.content: NumPy implementation of a multilayer perceptron

chapters.title: Backpropagation
chapters.content: Computational graphs, vanishing gradients

chapters.title: Training with PyTorch
chapters.content: Tensors, autograd, training loops, optimisers (SGD, Adam), regularisation, checkpoints

chapters.title: CNNs
chapters.content: Convolution, pooling, architectures, transfer learning

chapters.title: Sequences & Attention
chapters.content: RNN, LSTM and GRU, attention, the Transformer architecture

phases.math: Calculus (chain rule on computational graphs) · Linear algebra (matrix products, convolution) · Optimisation (stochastic gradient descent, Adam) · Probability (softmax, cross-entropy)

phases.name: Responsible AI
phases.focus: Explainability, fairness, the EU AI Act, model cards
phases.intro: Participants explain model predictions globally and locally, measure and mitigate bias, and document models for governance under the EU AI Act and data protection rules. Validated lab: a SHAP explanation and a fairness report for the phase 1 model, summarised in a model card.

chapters.title: Explainability
chapters.content: SHAP, LIME, feature importance

chapters.title: Bias, Fairness & Governance
chapters.content: Fairness metrics, the EU AI Act and data protection, model cards

phases.name: Reinforcement Learning
phases.focus: MDPs, dynamic programming, Q-learning, DQN, policy gradients
phases.intro: This optional module adds 9 h for groups who want it. Participants model decision problems as Markov decision processes, solve them with dynamic programming, then learn from experience with Q-learning and SARSA, deep Q-networks and policy-gradient methods. Validated lab: an agent trained with Q-learning and then with a DQN on a Gymnasium environment, with the learning curves compared.

chapters.title: RL & MDPs
chapters.content: Agent, environment, rewards, policies, Bellman equations

chapters.title: Dynamic Programming
chapters.content: Value iteration and policy iteration

chapters.title: Q-Learning & SARSA
chapters.content: Temporal-difference learning

chapters.title: Deep Q-Networks
chapters.content: Experience replay, target networks

chapters.title: Policy Gradients & Actor-Critic
chapters.content: REINFORCE, A2C, PPO overview

phases.math: Probability (Markov decision processes, expectations) · Dynamic programming (Bellman equations) · Calculus (policy gradient theorem, log-derivative trick)

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: An end-to-end machine learning project, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three carry a machine learning problem from framing to explanation on a provided dataset, reusing the phase labs, then present it as they would to a product team.

chapters.title: Framing & Exploration
chapters.content: Frame the problem and the metric, exploratory data analysis, split strategy

chapters.title: Models & Experiments
chapters.content: Feature pipeline, comparison of classical models and a deep learning model, all tracked in MLflow

chapters.title: Explain & Document
chapters.content: Explainability report, model card, short technical report

chapters.title: Presentation & Review
chapters.content: Presentation of the results and limits; questions and feedback

project.title: End-to-End Machine Learning Project
project.brief: A machine learning problem carried from framing and exploration to a feature pipeline, a comparison of classical models with a deep learning model, an explainability report and a model card, with every experiment tracked.
project.stack: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, XGBoost or LightGBM, PyTorch, MLflow, SHAP, JupyterLab
project.deliverable: Repository with notebooks and pipeline code, MLflow runs, explainability report, model card, presentation
